messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED — SLO breach detected for customer StratusHealth (VPC: sthealth-eu-west-2, Dedicated Pool: dp-42). p99 latency for text-generation endpoint at ~5.8s (SLO 1.5s). Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

maya_sre: picking this up. on-call for infra. I see the alert, routing to runbook 'vpc-dedicated-latency'. can someone paste the metric window?

noah_platform: digging in dashboards now — 5m p95 = 1.9s, p99 = 5.8s, avg 0.9s. error rate normal. throughput steady ~480 rps.

elena_engineering: looks like KC cache miss rate spiked for tenant sharding key 'sthealth-xx'. KV cache hit dropped from 92% -> 12% around 14:02 UTC.

raj_ml: that's suspicious — model variant is rdx-13b-quant. Sequence length distribution is normal. Could be noisy tenant causing KV thrash.

luis_support: StratusHealth reported slow responses to their app. Customer SRE (stratus_oncall) is in the thread. cc @sophie_am for AM handling.

sophie_am: I'm here, pinged customer. They're seeing front-end timeouts on a set of batch jobs hitting our generate API. They're concerned about SLAs. I'll keep them updated.

stratus_oncall: Confirmed. Our payment reconciliation workers are timing out on a nightly batch window. This started ~14:00 UTC for us. We're throttling retries to avoid cascading failures but need mitigation.

maya_sre: immediate mitigations: 1) isolate noisy tenant traffic in DP-42; 2) spin up a warm worker group in eu-west-1 as regional failover; 3) temporary rate-limit heavy endpoints for the tenant. I'll start 1 and 3 now.

noah_platform: isolating tenant via routing rule change. Applying route override to send sthealth-xx -> dp-42-noisy-shield pool. command: `redwoodctl route update --tenant sthealth-xx --pool dp-42-noisy-shield`

elena_engineering: adding a KV cache TTL bump and disabling cross-tenant caching for that tenant: patch applied to config service. snippet:

```
service.kv_cache.override["sthealth-xx"] = { enabled: false, ttl: 1s }
```

raj_ml: curious if batching parameters got changed — there's a recent autosuggest config in the tenant profile increasing max_batch_size to 64 at 13:59 UTC. that could explain latency when mixed with cache misses.

maya_sre: rollback of tenant batch config initiated. `redwoodctl tenants config rollback sthealth-xx --key max_batch_size --to 16`

luis_support: updated customer: we've isolated your noisy job and rolled back a recent batching config. Please confirm if you see improvement.

stratus_oncall: seeing partial improvement. p99 dropped to ~3.1s but still above SLO. Batch windows still heavy. We can throttle jobs on our side, but need guidance on long-term fix.

noah_platform: spinning up additional dedicated workers in eu-west-2 (dp-42-burst). autoscale request sent, ETA ~3m.

incident-bot: Pager duty: On-call escalation to eng-sre-team (priority P1) — paging maya_sre, noah_platform.

maya_sre: after warm capacity comes up, we should migrate the customer's high-volume jobs to dp-42-burst and enable KV prefill for their expected prefixes. I'll run a migration plan: 1) mark jobs as 'drain' on dp-42-noisy-shield 2) add route for heavy job path -> dp-42-burst 3) kick KV prefill worker.

elena_engineering: KV prefill kicked with partial prefixes. script: `scripts/prefill_kv.sh sthealth-xx /prefixes/batch-jobs`

raj_ml: running quick evals on DP-42 variants — rdx-13b-quant on dp-42-burst shows tail latency improvement in synthetic tests: p99 ~1.3s when cache warmed. Good signal.

noah_platform: dp-42-burst is up and accepting traffic. Swapping routing for heavy path now.

luis_support: Notified customer: we've moved heavy jobs to burst pool and started cache prefill. Monitoring for next 10m and will update.

stratus_oncall: Thanks — after migration p99 is ~1.4s for most calls, intermittent 2.1s spikes. Front-end no longer timing out. We're gradually re-enabling jobs.

maya_sre: marking incident as mitigated. Remaining work: a postmortem to understand why tenant-level config change got auto-deployed and how KV cache eviction occurred. I'll keep the war room open for handoff to eng for root cause.

sophie_am: I'll schedule a customer post-incident call for tomorrow 09:00 UTC and share a summary. Apologized to customer and offered 10% credits for the window.

elena_engineering: immediate follow-ups for eng: 1) audit tenant config rollout pipeline (who/what triggered max_batch_size change), 2) KV eviction tuning, 3) add a guard in routing that prevents noisy tenant from using cross-tenant caching.

raj_ml: add regression test for batching config + cache behavior on staging.

maya_sre: handing off to eng oncall for PM: @elena_engineering you own the RCA. I'll update status to 'mitigated' in the incident tracker.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Total impact window ~14:00–14:18 UTC. P99 peak 5.8s -> baseline 1.4s after mitigations.

luis_support: Customer confirms reduced impact. Closing loop with account exec.

stratus_oncall: Confirmed stable. Thanks for fast response. We'll follow up on config audit from our side too.

sophie_am: final note: please add the internal postmortem link here when ready. :thumbsup:

maya_sre: Will do. closing thread for now but will reopen if regression.
